\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Extension}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Cube.Reverse.Extension
\section{Overview}
Reverse Bonami--Beckner hypercontractivity extends to finite real exponents on both sides of zero, including the geometric-mean and exponent-one cases.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Extension to finite real exponents]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.extend_reverse_bonami_beckner}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsNonnegative, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ReverseMoments.expect_normalized_rpow_eq_one, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ReverseMoments.expect_rpow_pos, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean_noise_antitone, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lpMean_of_pos, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_compose, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_const_mul, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_eq_kernel_sum, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.reverse_bonami_beckner_positive_sharp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.reverse_holder, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.expect_eq_fintypeExpect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp_self_adjoint, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight, BooleanAnalysis.walsh_expansion}
\difficulty{7}
Let $q\le p\le1$, $q<1$, $0\le\rho\le1$, and $\rho^2\le(1-p)/(1-q)$. Every $f:\{0,1\}^n\to[0,\infty)$ satisfies $M_q(T_\rho f)\ge M_p(f)$. For nonnegative functions $u$, the extended mean is $M_r(u)=(\E u^r)^{1/r}$ when $r>0$; the same formula applies for $r<0$ when $u$ is positive everywhere. For positive $u$, $M_0(u)=\exp(\E\log u)$; if $r\le0$ and $u$ has a zero, $M_r(u)=0$. All expectations are uniform. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{lemma}
